subject: Renewal pricing: term extension & inflation protection
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@pacificretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@pacificretail.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — term extension and inflation protection

Jordan —

Thanks for the renewal notice. We're generally happy with Redwood but two things are blocking our Finance team: ongoing inflation in compute costs and uncertainty about next-year budgets. Pacific Retail is interested in a 18–24 month term to lock price, but only if we can get a limited price protection and some one-time credits for migration/validation work.

Questions: can Redwood offer a price-hold for at least 18 months? Would you consider a tiered discount tied to a committed usage increase? And do you have flexibility on an onboarding/validation credit?

Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Best,
Elena Morales
VP of Engineering, Pacific Retail
Attachments: none
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@pacificretail.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@pacificretail.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — term extension and inflation protection

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and context. We can work with this. High level options I can put on the table for our call:

- 12-month term (shorter) with a 10% one-time usage credit and a 6% list-rate discount for the year.
- 18-month term (mid) with a 10% discount year 1, 5% discount year 2, plus a $45k usage credit for onboarding/validation; we would ask for a moderate commit increase (approx +25% from current run-rate).
- 24-month term (long) with a fixed price-hold (no inflation pass-through for 24 months) but smaller upfront credit ($25k) and a slightly lower discount (5% fixed).

I can share numbers and a quick spreadsheet. Can you do Wed Aug 19 11am PT for a 30-min alignment? If that's tight, propose two times and Raj/you can pick.

Thanks — Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: PR_Renewal_Counter_20260817.xlsx (pricing scenarios)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Pacific Retail renewal — proposed concession sketches

Team — quick sync. Pacific Retail asked for inflation protection and a credit. I spoke to Elena and proposed three options (see sheet). Their preference is 18–24 months with a price-hold if possible.

My recommended counter to present on Wednesday:
1) Primary: 18-month term, 10% discount Y1, 5% discount Y2, $45k usage credit applied as invoice credit over first 3 months, commit uplift target +25%. Include standard SLA and retention terms.
2) Secondary: 24-month term with fixed price-hold, 5% standard discount, $25k onboarding credit, require commitment increase +35% and annual true-up.

Constraints / asks: finance wants credits as usage credits (not cash refunds). Legal will need a short MSA amendment for the price-hold clause (no inflation pass-through). Ops flags: verify capacity in us-west for expected burst months.

Can finance/legal/ops please confirm if the credit structure and price-hold language are acceptable? If so I'll present the 18-month primary to customer and push for a signed amendment.

Thanks — Jordan
Attachments: PR_Renewal_Counter_20260817.xlsx
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Pacific Retail renewal — proposed concession sketches

Jordan — thanks for the draft. Quick notes from Pricing & Finance:

- Usage credit is preferred (applied to invoices) — agree $45k applied over 90 days is fine.
- Require the commit uplift to be explicit in the amendment: define committed units (tokens/embedding units) and a clear true-up mechanism for underusage. We should avoid open-ended uplift asks.
- For the price-hold clause: Legal wants a narrowly scoped clause: price-hold applies to the model endpoint list prices for covered SKUs and excludes third-party licensing costs or region-specific taxes. Also include a termination carve-out if disruptions exceed 3 consecutive days of downtime (SLA breach).

Operationally David: please confirm capacity in us-west for expected Black Friday window (they called out retail spikes).

If all agree, approve the 18-month plan and Jordan can take to customer.

— Stephanie
Director, Pricing & GTM Finance
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@pacificretail.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@pacificretail.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — term extension and inflation protection

Elena / Raj — thanks again for the conversation earlier this week. Following internal review we've prepared a formal counter that balances your desire for price stability with the commercial constraints Stephanie flagged. Summary below and the amendment is attached for review (MSA_Amendment_Draft.pdf).

Our counter (preferred option):
- Term: 18 months (Sep 1, 2026 — Feb 28, 2028)
- Pricing: 10% list discount for first 12 months; 5% list discount for months 13–18
- Credit: $45,000 usage credit, applied as invoice credit over first 3 billing cycles
- Commit: target committed units = current run-rate * 1.25 (explicit SKU/units defined in attached spreadsheet). Annual true-up applies at month 12; underusage will trigger prorated reconciliation per amendment.
- Price-hold: Redwood will not increase list prices for the covered SKUs during the 18-month term except for region-specific taxes or third-party pass-throughs. The price-hold excludes material third-party licensing increases; see amendment section 2.3 for exclusions.
- SLA carve-out: if Redwood experiences more than 3 consecutive days of platform downtime attributable to Redwood, Pacific Retail may request termination rights (limited to core accounts discussed in amendment).

Next steps: I can send a DocuSign amendment if you want to proceed; legal has drafted the narrow price-hold language and finance will apply the $45k as usage credit on the next invoice upon signature. If you want to tweak commit definitions or billing cadence we can adjust the spreadsheet.

Please let me know if you want the DocuSign link now.

Best — Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_Amendment_Draft.pdf (amendment draft)
